items.title: European Commission hit by AI-powered cyberattack
items.summary: The European Commission recently fell victim to a cyberattack that was reportedly caused by an "AI-generated tool." Investigations are still underway.

items.title: It’s time to retire vanity security dashboards
items.summary: In this Help Net Security video, Abdul Khadir Mahamed, OT Security Architect at Estée Lauder Companies, explains why security teams should retire vanity dashboards in IT and OT environments.

items.summary: Maria Deutscher / SiliconANGLE : BrightAI, which uses AI to help industrial companies detect malfunctioning equipment, raised $97M led by Smith Point, bringing its total funding to $184M — BrightAI Inc., a startup that helps industrial companies detect malfunctioning equipment, has raised $97 million in funding.

items.title: OpenAI outlines isolated deployments for Daybreak Red security investigations
items.summary: Daybreak Red is OpenAI’s access tier for authorized security research and testing. A deployment guide outlines a reference architecture for running supervised investigations in an isolated environment, including safety controls, configuration and monitoring. Source

items.title: Get started with Daybreak Blue: OpenAI shows the onboarding process
items.summary: Daybreak Blue is OpenAI’s online access tier for approved cybersecurity work using AI. A new onboarding demo introduces the setup process, while OpenAI’s guidance details how organizations can enable access for API projects and Codex users. Source

items.title: OpenAI demos a first scan with the Codex Security Plugin
items.summary: The Codex Security Plugin is an AI-assisted tool for scanning code for security issues. OpenAI has published a product demo showing how to get started and review the results of a scan. Source

items.title: OpenAI’s Performance Factory uses Codex to investigate ChatGPT slowdowns
items.summary: OpenAI has detailed Performance Factory, a cloud-based system that uses Codex AI coding agents to investigate performance regressions in services including ChatGPT. Its first workflow tracked more than 1,700 investigations and identified root causes in over 600 cases in just over three months.

items.title: Axelera Titania targets AI inference in existing air-cooled racks
items.summary: Axelera AI’s Titania is a new chip architecture designed to run trained AI models in enterprise data centers. The company says a server using the chips could draw about 6 kilowatts and fit into existing air-cooled racks, potentially making on-premises AI inference more accessible without liquid-cooling upgrades. Source

items.title: Trump fires national cyber director after wave of tech outages
items.summary: Cybersecurity expert and former NSA hacker David Kennedy discusses a reported new cyberattack amid a series of US technology outages. National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross has stepped down, while Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has reportedly been sidelined from television appearances.

items.title: Anthropic’s record IPO puts AI growth to the public-market test
items.summary: Anthropic’s $81 billion IPO sent its shares up 17% on their first trading day, valuing the Claude maker at roughly $1.76 trillion. Source

items.title: AI agent API security hasn’t caught up with agents already running in production
items.summary: Postman asked nearly 9,000 developers, architects and executives how they’re handling AI agents, and the answers tell a familiar story. Companies put the new thing to work first and left the question of who holds the keys for later.

items.title: New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It
items.summary: A newly disclosed unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock lets someone with physical access to a locked Windows computer start programs without signing in. Whoever uses it gets only a limited account, not administrator control of the machine.

items.title: Google is pushing OEMs against GrapheneOS and bootloader unlocking
items.summary: Comments

items.title: Liqid launches managed AI inference service with pooled GPU memory
items.summary: Liqid pools data center GPUs and memory so servers can be configured for different AI inference workloads. At SC26, the company announced Liqid as a Service, a fully managed offering dedicated to a single customer, and said it is moving toward preconfigured appliances. Source

items.title: PHP 8.6 changes session defaults and adds new language features
items.summary: PHP 8.6, the latest release of the server-side language used by web applications, enables stricter session defaults that may affect existing login flows. It also adds partial function application and tools for timing and event loops.

items.title: Microsoft Copilot SDK 2.0 runs multiple AI agent sessions in one process
items.summary: Microsoft Copilot SDK lets developers add AI agents to applications running locally or in the cloud. Version 2.0 can host multiple users’ sessions in a shared application process instead of starting a separate environment for each conversation.

items.title: Open-source platform StarlingX 13.0 turns edge servers into network switches
items.summary: StarlingX, an open-source Linux-based platform for running distributed clouds at edge sites, now lets servers switch traffic where a local router is unavailable. Version 13.0 also adds an optional certificate authority, a new Kubernetes routing option and faster recovery for remote sites. Source

items.title: Windows 11 26H1 KB5132265 preview brings Cloud rebuild and IPv6 translation
items.summary: Windows 11 26H1’s KB5132265 preview introduces Cloud rebuild for reinstalling Windows without USB media, alongside File Explorer customization and IPv6 compatibility improvements.

items.title: Windows 11 lock screen flaw reportedly exposes BitLocker-protected PCs
items.summary: A newly disclosed Windows 11 lock screen flaw could let someone with physical access interact with a locked, signed-in PC using only a keyboard. Researcher Abdelhamid Naceri says the technique can reach Windows Settings through Narrator, potentially allowing software to run despite BitLocker protection.

items.title: Apple is hiring to build AI agent that can browse, code and control apps
items.summary: Apple is hiring an engineer to lead development of an AI agent designed to browse the web, write code and work across apps. The job listing describes software that could plan multistep tasks and delegate parts of them to specialized agents. Source

items.title: Microsoft Agent Framework attack traced to release pipeline certificate
items.summary: Wiz researchers say the attacker behind the malicious Microsoft Agent Framework Python releases appears to have used a certificate and private key associated with Microsoft’s release pipeline. Agent Framework is a toolkit for building AI agents; its compromised packages stole credentials whenever Python started.

items.title: Microsoft Ignite 2026 adds agent access to on-premises apps and Azure backup protection
items.summary: Microsoft’s Ignite 2026 announcements include a preview that lets Windows 365 agents access on-premises applications using agent identities, alongside newly available protections for Azure workloads and backups.

items.title: Gemini’s Mac app can now control desktop apps for you
items.summary: Google’s Gemini is an AI assistant available on macOS and other platforms. Its Mac app can now use local applications and websites to carry out multistep tasks in the background. The feature is available in the United States to users with a Google AI subscription. Source

also_covered_by.title: Gemini app for Mac can now handle your repetitive multi-step tasks

items.title: Microsoft Teams to drop iOS 17 support, but existing apps will keep working
items.summary: Microsoft Teams will end support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 starting in mid-December 2026, with the rollout expected to finish by early January 2027. Existing installations will continue to work, but newer Teams releases will require iOS 18 or iPadOS 18 or later. Source

items.title: VMware vCenter zero-day exploited by Armory Castle since September
items.summary: A China-linked espionage group exploited a critical VMware vCenter authentication bypass in September, more than two months before Broadcom released a fix, according to Mandiant.

items.title: VMware vCenter bypass exploited before patch; separate KVM flaw exposes host memory
items.summary: A suspected espionage group exploited the critical VMware vCenter authentication bypass more than two months before Broadcom released a fix, according to Google’s threat intelligence team.

items.title: Cloudflare explains where its proxy blocks nginx2root attacks—and where it doesn’t
items.summary: Cloudflare says its HTTP proxy blocks attacks against the HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 flaws in nginx2root , provided attackers cannot reach the nginx server directly. The proxy, which sits between clients and web servers, terminates their connections rather than forwarding the malicious protocol frames.

items.title: Most CIOs and CISOs expect to contain attacks, though few can reach their gear right away
items.summary: Most organizations can’t quickly get secure management access to their own critical network infrastructure once the primary network goes down. Opengear surveyed 514 CIOs and CISOs and only a small share said they could get that access immediately or close to it.

items.summary: The company counts physicists, a former journalist and an associate of the pope among its guiding lights The paper fortunes of Anthropic’s seven co-founders reached a total of more than $180bn on Thursday as shares in their company started trading at a price ahead of expectations.

items.title: PHP 8.6.0 released
items.summary: Version 8.6.0 of PHP has been released. Notable changes in this release include a polling API, a new clamp() function, a SortDirection enum, and a \Time\Duration class. See " What's new in 8.6 " for more on new features, and the changelog for a full list of changes.

items.title: Drupal Patches Critical Installer Flaw That Could Give Unauthenticated Attackers Control of Sites
items.summary: Under specific conditions, a critical vulnerability in Drupal core can allow an attacker without login credentials to use the built-in installer to attempt to reinstall a site. That can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution, and the project rates the vulnerable configurations as uncommon.
